title: Tax Mitigation & Deferral Strategies for High-Income Individuals
desc: Tax mitigation and deferral strategies for complex, high-stakes situations: oil and gas, PPLI, income shifting and real estate, each tailored to the client and reviewed by tax counsel.
text: tax strategy where others see walls, paratum sees doors. its tax work is for situations where standard planning has run out of answers: a large gain, a high-income year, a concentrated position, an inheritance. mitigation and deferral mitigation reduces the tax owed. deferral moves it to a later year, when rates, income or circumstances may be more favorable, and keeps the capital working in the meantime. most strategies do some of both. the right mix depends on the client's income, assets, state of residence and plans, which is why every structure starts from the client's facts rather than a product. when it matters most the sale of a business, real estate or a concentrated stock position a year of unusually high ordinary income recurring high income from a practice or operating business a family with income spread unevenly across generations or states a large portfolio growing in a fully taxable account core strategies oil and gas direct energy investments whose drilling costs are largely deductible in the first year. read more ppli investments held inside a life insurance policy, growing without current tax. read more income shifting moving income to family members, trusts or entities taxed at lower rates. read more real estate accelerated depreciation, exchanges and fund structures that defer gain. read more additional strategies charitable remainder trusts, which convert an appreciated asset into an income stream and a charitable deduction; installment sales, which spread a gain over the years in which payment is received; the qualified small business stock exclusion, which can exclude much of the gain on founder shares in a qualifying company; and qualified opportunity funds, which defer gain reinvested in designated communities. for business sales and companies with unused losses or credits, see m a advisory . tailored, and reviewed by counsel no structure is sold off the shelf. each is designed around the client's circumstances and reviewed by the client's own tax counsel before it is put in place, and implemented by licensed professionals. paratum stays involved afterward, because a structure that is not maintained can lose the treatment it was built for. paratum does not provide tax or legal advice. results depend on each client's facts and current law. see disclosures . oil and gas

title: Oil and Gas Tax Deductions & Intangible Drilling Costs
desc: How direct oil and gas investments work as a tax strategy: the intangible drilling cost deduction, depletion, working versus royalty interests, risks, and who they fit.
text: oil and gas a direct investment in oil and gas drilling is one of the few places the tax code still allows most of an investment to be deducted in the year it is made. key applications intangible drilling cost deductions offsetting ordinary income depletion allowances working and royalty interests who may benefit investors with high ordinary income in the current year, from a practice, a business or a liquidity event, who can hold an illiquid investment for several years and accept the risks of drilling. because a working interest is not treated as a passive activity for this purpose, the deduction can offset active income, which is what makes it unusual. our role paratum designs the strategy and coordinates the specialists who carry it out: energy tax counsel, the client's cpa, independent petroleum engineers for reserve reviews, and established operators. technical considerations what it is the investor takes a working interest in one or more wells through a partnership or program run by an operator. most of the cost of drilling, the labor, fuel, chemicals and site preparation known as intangible drilling costs (idcs), is generally deductible in the year incurred. equipment costs are depreciated over several years. once a well produces, a portion of its income is sheltered by the depletion allowance. how it works paratum reviews the client's income and the size of the deduction that makes sense. it identifies operators and programs, and coordinates diligence on their track record, geology and terms. the client's cpa and tax counsel confirm the expected treatment before any commitment. the client invests directly with the operator; the deduction flows through on the program's tax reporting. working and royalty interests a working interest carries the costs, the deductions and the operational risk. a royalty interest receives a share of production without bearing costs, and offers depletion but not the drilling deduction. many investors hold both over time. risks and considerations wells can be dry or produce less than expected. commodity prices move. the investment is illiquid, and a working interest can carry liability that is usually addressed through the program's structure. deductions can be recaptured on sale, and the alternative minimum tax and state rules can change the result. the quality of the operator matters more than the tax benefit. frequently asked questions how much of the investment is deductible in the first year? it depends on the program's mix of intangible and tangible costs and the timing of drilling. many programs target a majority of the investment as deductible in the first year; the client's tax counsel confirms the figure for a specific program. is this the same as an oil and gas fund? not necessarily. many funds hold royalty or non-operated interests that do not pass through the drilling deduction. the structure determines the tax result. illustrative information only, not tax advice or an offer of any investment. see disclosures . ppli

title: Private Placement Life Insurance (PPLI) Explained
desc: Private placement life insurance holds investments inside a life insurance policy so they grow without current tax and pass income-tax-free at death. How it works, the rules, and who it suits.
text: ppli private placement life insurance places an investment portfolio inside a life insurance policy, where it can grow without current income tax and pass to heirs income-tax-free. key applications tax-deferred investment growth tax-efficient portfolio structuring multigenerational wealth transfer estate and trust integration who may benefit individuals and families with substantial investable assets, a long horizon and a portfolio that generates heavy annual tax, particularly from income-producing or actively traded strategies. it is often combined with a trust so the policy sits outside the taxable estate as well. our role paratum designs the strategy and coordinates the specialists who carry it out: insurance carriers that offer private placement policies, licensed agents, insurance-dedicated fund managers, trust counsel and the client's cpa. policies are placed only by licensed professionals. technical considerations what it is ppli is a variable universal life policy offered privately to qualified buyers. the premium is invested in insurance-dedicated funds or separately managed accounts, which can include hedge fund, private credit and other strategies that are normally tax-inefficient. insurance costs can be lower than in comparable retail policies, depending on the carrier and structure, because the policy is designed for investment rather than for the death benefit. how it works paratum assesses whether the client's assets, horizon and goals justify a policy. it coordinates the carrier, a licensed agent, the investment managers and the trust structure. premiums are paid in, usually over several years, and invested inside the policy. growth inside the policy is not currently taxed; the death benefit passes to beneficiaries generally free of income tax, and policy loans can provide access during life. legal and regulatory considerations the policy must meet the tax code's definition of life insurance and its diversification requirements, and the policyholder may not direct the specific investments, a limit known as the investor control doctrine. a policy funded too quickly can become a modified endowment contract, which changes how withdrawals and loans are taxed. these rules are why design and ongoing administration matter. frequently asked questions how does ppli work? qualifying investments are held inside a privately issued life insurance policy, where they can grow without current income tax. the death benefit generally passes to beneficiaries free of income tax. who is ppli designed for? generally, qualified purchasers and accredited investors with substantial investable assets, a long horizon and a portfolio that produces significant annual tax. what are the costs? insurance charges, carrier and premium-tax charges, and the fees of the underlying investment managers. costs can be lower than in comparable retail policies, depending on the carrier and structure, and must be weighed against the expected tax savings. what can go wrong? a policy that fails the tax code s definition of life insurance, breaches the diversification rules or the investor control doctrine, or is funded too quickly can lose some or all of its tax benefits. careful design and administration are essential. paratum is not an insurance agency and does not sell insurance. see disclosures . income shifting

title: Income Shifting Strategies: Trusts, Partnerships & Entities
desc: Income shifting moves income to family members, trusts or entities taxed at lower rates or in lower-tax states. Family partnerships, non-grantor trusts and entity structures explained.
text: income shifting income shifting moves income from the person who would pay the highest rate to a family member, trust or entity that pays less, within rules that require the shift to be real. key applications family limited partnerships and llcs non-grantor trusts business entity structuring intergenerational ownership transfers state income tax planning who may benefit families with high income concentrated in one generation, owners of closely held businesses, and residents of high-tax states with investment income that need not be earned there. our role paratum designs the strategy and coordinates the specialists who carry it out: tax and trust counsel, the client's cpa, independent trustees and valuation firms. technical considerations principal approaches family limited partnerships and llcs a family partnership holds investments or a business. interests are transferred to children or trusts, and the income follows the ownership. transfers can also qualify for valuation discounts for gift and estate tax purposes. non-grantor trusts a trust that is taxed as its own taxpayer can, when properly designed and located, reduce or avoid state income tax on investment income, and distributions to beneficiaries in lower brackets carry the income with them. entity structures the choice of entity, and how owners and family members who genuinely work in a business are compensated, changes how and where income is taxed. management companies and holding structures can also separate income streams that are taxed differently. risks and considerations the tax law ignores shifts that lack substance: income from services is taxed to the person who performs them, children's investment income can be taxed at their parents' rates, and states pursue trusts they consider resident. control, ownership and economics must actually change. paratum's work is to design a structure that will hold up, with counsel who will defend it. frequently asked questions what is income shifting? legitimately moving income-producing assets or business interests to family members, trusts or entities that are taxed at lower rates or in lower-tax states. can a trust reduce state income tax? a properly structured non-grantor trust may avoid state income tax on investment income, depending on where the trust is administered, who its trustees and beneficiaries are, and where the income is sourced. can income shifting be combined with estate planning? yes. transferring ownership interests can serve both purposes, moving income today and future appreciation out of the estate. what limits apply? the assignment-of-income doctrine, economic substance requirements, gift tax, the kiddie tax and state residency rules for trusts all have to be addressed. not tax advice. see disclosures . real estate

title: Real Estate Tax Deferral: Cost Segregation, 1031 Exchanges & DSTs
desc: Real estate tax strategies: cost segregation and bonus depreciation, 1031 exchanges, Delaware statutory trusts and opportunity zone funds, explained for owners and investors.
text: real estate real estate remains the most flexible tax asset most families own. the deductions can be accelerated, the gain can be deferred, and with planning it can pass to heirs at a stepped-up basis. key applications cost segregation and bonus depreciation section 1031 exchanges delaware statutory trusts qualified opportunity funds our role paratum designs the strategy and coordinates the specialists who carry it out: cost segregation engineers, qualified intermediaries for exchanges, dst and fund sponsors, real estate tax counsel and lenders. technical considerations cost segregation and bonus depreciation a cost segregation study separates a building's components, such as fixtures, finishes and site work, from the structure itself. those components are depreciated over five to fifteen years rather than twenty-seven and a half or thirty-nine, and may qualify for bonus depreciation in the first year. the result is a large early deduction that can offset other income where the owner qualifies. 1031 exchanges selling investment property and reinvesting the proceeds in like-kind property within the statutory deadlines defers the gain. exchanges can be repeated over a lifetime, and the deferred gain may never be taxed if the property passes at death. delaware statutory trusts a dst lets an owner exchange into a fractional interest in institutional property, such as a portfolio of apartments or industrial buildings, without managing it. it suits owners who want to keep deferring but stop operating. opportunity zone funds capital gains from any source can be reinvested in a qualified opportunity fund, deferring the original gain, and appreciation on the new investment held long enough can be excluded from tax. frequently asked questions what is cost segregation? an engineering study that identifies building components eligible for shorter depreciation periods, accelerating deductions into the early years of ownership. how does a 1031 exchange work? investment or business real estate is sold and the proceeds reinvested in like-kind property through a qualified intermediary, within 45 days to identify and 180 days to close, deferring the gain. what is a delaware statutory trust? a trust that holds institutional real estate and sells fractional interests that can qualify as replacement property in a 1031 exchange, letting an owner keep deferring without managing property. can real estate losses offset other income? only within the passive activity rules. real estate professionals who materially participate, and certain short-term rental owners, may use losses against other income; others generally carry them forward. not tax advice or an offer of any security. see disclosures . m a advisory

title: Tax-Efficient M&A Advisory & Tax Attribute Monetization
desc: M&A advisory with tax at the center: sell-side and buy-side structuring, and the identification, valuation and monetization of tax attributes such as NOLs and credits.
text: m a advisory in most transactions tax is settled at the end. paratum starts with it, because the structure of a deal often moves after-tax proceeds more than the price does. sell-side the most valuable work happens one to two years before a sale. paratum helps owners decide between an asset sale and a stock sale, use installment terms and rollover equity (keeping a stake in the buyer to defer tax on part of the price), move shares into trusts before value is fixed, and qualify for the small business stock exclusion where it applies. it then coordinates the tax counsel and advisers who carry the transaction. buy-side for acquirers, structure determines whether the purchase price becomes depreciable basis. paratum works on structures that give the buyer a step-up in the basis of the assets acquired, and on how the price is allocated among them, so the deductions that follow are as large as the facts allow. tax attribute monetization tax attributes are tax assets a company carries: net operating losses (nols, past losses that can offset future income), capital loss carryforwards and tax credits. many sit unused on the books of companies that will never earn enough to absorb them. paratum identifies these attributes, values them, and finds a buyer, merger partner or structure that can use them. section 382 caps how much of a company's nols can be used each year after a change in ownership, so the value of an attribute depends heavily on how the transaction is built. paratum also advises on selling eligible clean-energy credits for cash under the transferability rules. restructurings and recapitalizations a restructuring or bankruptcy can erase tax attributes or preserve them. paratum works with restructuring counsel so that losses and credits survive a reorganization where possible, and become part of the value recovered. our role paratum designs the strategy and coordinates the specialists who carry it out: m a and tax counsel, accountants for quality-of-earnings and tax due diligence, valuation firms, lenders, and registered investment banks where a transaction requires one. frequently asked questions can a company's nols be sold on their own? not directly. losses belong to the company, so they are realized through a merger, acquisition or restructuring that lets a profitable business use them, within the section 382 limits. when should a business owner start planning a sale? ideally one to two years ahead. many of the most effective steps, such as gifts to trusts or changes in entity, must be taken before a buyer is in view. can tax credits be sold? certain federal clean-energy credits, and some state credits, can be transferred to an unrelated buyer for cash under the applicable rules. does paratum execute securities transactions? no. securities transactions and regulated investment banking work are carried out by registered firms. paratum is not a broker-dealer or investment bank and does not offer securities. see disclosures . asset protection

title: Asset Protection, Trust & Succession Planning
desc: Asset protection and succession planning for high net worth families: domestic and offshore trusts, layered entities, fiduciary oversight and estate continuity, put in place before they are needed.
text: asset protection protection is strongest when it is built before it is needed. a structure in place years before a claim is hard to reach; the same structure put in place after a claim can be undone. why timing matters transfers made to avoid a creditor who already exists, or one who is reasonably foreseeable, can be reversed by a court under fraudulent transfer law. planning done in calm years, for legitimate reasons such as estate planning and business succession, is far more durable. paratum's protection work is therefore mostly preventive, and part of a family's broader plan rather than a reaction to a lawsuit. four areas protection structures domestic and offshore trusts, layered entities and equity stripping. read more trusts and fiduciary choosing and overseeing trustees, trust situs and directed trusts. read more succession dynasty trusts, estate freezes and passing a business intact. read more pre-litigation planning reviewing exposure and repositioning assets before a dispute begins. read more our approach paratum maps what a family owns, how it is held and where it is exposed, then designs the combination of structures that fits. asset protection counsel drafts the documents, independent trustees and trust companies hold the assets, and paratum coordinates them and keeps the structure maintained, because protection that is not respected in practice does not hold. paratum does not provide legal advice. structures are established by licensed counsel. see disclosures . protection structures

title: Asset Protection Trusts, Offshore Trusts & Equity Stripping
desc: Asset protection structures explained: domestic asset protection trusts in Nevada, South Dakota and Delaware, Cook Islands and Nevis trusts, layered LLCs and equity stripping.
text: protection structures no single structure addresses every exposure. a durable plan combines several, each established for a legitimate purpose, well before any claim, and maintained with care. key applications domestic asset protection trusts offshore asset protection trusts layered llcs and holding companies equity stripping ownership privacy our role paratum designs the strategy and coordinates the specialists who carry it out: domestic and offshore asset protection counsel, independent trustees and trust companies, lenders, and the client's cpa for the reporting that follows. technical considerations domestic asset protection trusts several states, among them nevada, south dakota and delaware, allow a person to create an irrevocable trust of which they remain a discretionary beneficiary, with assets protected from future creditors after a waiting period. nevada's two-year period is among the shortest. a trust of this kind works best for a resident of, or assets located in, a state that recognizes it. offshore trusts trusts in jurisdictions such as the cook islands and nevis do not enforce u.s. judgments, apply short limitation periods and place a high burden of proof on creditors, who must bring a new case locally. they are among the strongest protections available, though their effectiveness depends on the jurisdiction, the timing and the facts. they cost more and carry strict irs reporting obligations, and like any structure they work only when established well before a claim exists. layered entities limited liability companies formed in states with strong charging order protection, such as wyoming, nevada and delaware, separate risky assets from safe ones and limit a creditor of an owner to distributions the company chooses to make. holding each property or business in its own entity keeps a claim against one from reaching the others. equity stripping equity stripping places legitimate, documented debt against an asset, typically real estate or a business, so that little equity remains exposed. the borrowed funds are invested elsewhere, often in protected structures. it must involve real lenders or real obligations on commercial terms; arrangements that exist only on paper can be disregarded. privacy ownership structures that keep a family's name off public records do not by themselves protect assets, but they reduce the chance of being targeted in the first place. frequently asked questions what is a domestic asset protection trust? an irrevocable trust, available in states such as nevada, south dakota and delaware, of which the creator can remain a discretionary beneficiary while assets are protected from future creditors after a waiting period. what is an offshore asset protection trust? a trust governed by the law of a jurisdiction such as the cook islands or nevis, which does not enforce u.s. judgments and makes it difficult and expensive for a creditor to reach the assets. u.s. tax and reporting obligations still apply. is asset protection legal? yes, when it is done before a claim exists or is foreseeable, for legitimate reasons, and with full tax reporting. transfers made to defeat a known creditor can be reversed. can a structure guarantee protection? no. effectiveness depends on timing, jurisdiction, how the structure is administered and the law that applies. layering several structures makes recovery harder and more costly for a claimant. not legal advice. see disclosures . trusts and fiduciary

title: Trust & Fiduciary Services: Trustees, Directed Trusts & Trust Situs
desc: Choosing and overseeing trustees and trust companies, directed trusts, trust situs in Nevada, South Dakota and Delaware, and private trust companies for families.
text: trusts and fiduciary a trust is only as good as the people who run it. paratum helps families choose trustees, design how authority is divided, and oversee the trust for as long as it lasts. key applications trustee selection and succession directed trusts trust situs and migration private trust companies ongoing trustee oversight our role paratum coordinates trust counsel, independent trustees, trust companies and investment professionals so the structure stays aligned with the family s objectives. trustee services are provided by qualified independent fiduciaries. technical considerations choosing a trustee family members know the family but may lack independence or expertise; banks offer permanence but often limited flexibility; independent trust companies sit between the two. paratum helps match the trustee to the trust's purpose, and coordinates successor trustees so the trust never stalls. directed trusts in a directed trust, the duties a single trustee would normally hold are divided. an investment adviser directs the portfolio, a distribution adviser decides payments, and an administrative trustee keeps the records. families keep a trusted adviser in charge of investments while gaining a professional trustee in a favorable state. trust situs where a trust is based determines the law that governs it, its state income tax, how long it may last and how well it protects its assets. nevada, south dakota and delaware lead on all four. an existing trust can often be moved to a better situs through decanting or a change of trustee. private trust companies for larger families, a private trust company owned by the family can act as trustee for all of its trusts, keeping decisions in family hands under a formal governance structure. ongoing oversight paratum reviews trustee performance, fees, investment results and compliance with the trust's terms, and coordinates changes when the family's circumstances or the law move. frequently asked questions what is a directed trust? a trust that divides duties among a trustee and named advisers, so that investments, distributions and administration can each be handled by the party best suited to them. why does trust situs matter? the state where a trust is based governs its law, its state income tax, how long it can last and how well it protects assets. can an existing trust be changed? often. depending on its terms and state law, a trust may be modified, moved to a new state or decanted into a new trust with better terms. does paratum act as trustee? no. trustee services are provided by qualified independent trustees and trust companies. paratum helps select and oversee them. paratum is not a trustee or trust company. see disclosures . succession

title: Succession Planning for Family Wealth: Dynasty Trusts & Estate Freezes
desc: Succession planning for families and business owners: dynasty trusts, estate freezes such as GRATs and sales to grantor trusts, family limited partnerships and family governance.
text: succession succession planning decides whether wealth built in one generation reaches the next intact, and whether the next generation is ready to hold it. key applications dynasty trusts estate freezes family limited partnerships business succession family governance our role paratum coordinates estate counsel, tax professionals, valuation specialists and independent fiduciaries into one succession plan that reflects both the family s finances and its wishes. technical considerations dynasty trusts a dynasty trust holds assets for children, grandchildren and later generations, outside each of their estates. in states that allow trusts to last for centuries, assets can compound across generations without estate tax at each death, and with protection from beneficiaries' creditors and divorces. estate freezes an estate freeze fixes the value of an asset in the senior generation's estate and passes future growth to heirs. grantor retained annuity trusts (grats) and sales to intentionally defective grantor trusts are the common tools; both are most effective with assets expected to appreciate, such as a business before a sale. family partnerships holding assets in a family limited partnership or llc allows interests to be transferred gradually while control stays with the senior generation, and transferred interests can qualify for valuation discounts. business succession passing an operating business means deciding who will own it, who will run it, and how those who do not take part are treated fairly. paratum coordinates the legal, tax and valuation work and the agreements that make the transition stable. family governance family constitutions, councils and education for heirs give a family a way to make decisions together and prepare the next generation for responsibility, which often matters more than any document. frequently asked questions what is a dynasty trust? a trust designed to hold assets for several generations outside each beneficiary s taxable estate, often with protection from creditors and divorce. what is an estate freeze? a strategy that fixes the value of an asset in the senior generation s estate and passes future appreciation to heirs, commonly through a grat or a sale to a grantor trust. when should business succession planning begin? years before a transition. early planning leaves room to address tax, governance and management continuity on the family s own timetable. does succession planning include family governance? it should. governance agreements, family councils and education for heirs set out how decisions are made and prepare the next generation. not legal or tax advice. see disclosures . pre-litigation planning

title: Pre-Litigation Asset Protection for Professionals & Business Owners
desc: Pre-litigation asset protection: reviewing exposure and repositioning assets before a dispute begins, for physicians, executives, business owners and real estate holders.
text: pre-litigation planning responsible wealth preservation begins with understanding and managing financial exposure before disputes arise. paratum coordinates lawful preventive strategies designed to protect assets and support long-term financial security. key applications personal and business exposure reviews separating operating and investment assets entity restructuring insurance and statutory exemption reviews preventive trust planning who may benefit physicians and other professionals with malpractice exposure; executives and directors; owners of operating businesses with employees, vehicles or premises; real estate investors; and anyone whose wealth makes them a target out of proportion to their risk. our role paratum s role is preventive strategy and coordination. independent counsel evaluates the exposure and puts the structures in place; litigation, where it arises, is handled by litigation counsel. technical considerations what it involves an exposure review: which assets are reachable, through which claims, and in which states. separation of risky assets from safe ones, and of each business or property into its own entity. use of the protections the law already provides, such as retirement accounts, homestead and insurance. trusts and other structures for what remains exposed, put in place while no claim exists. legal and regulatory considerations moving assets after a claim arises, or when one is foreseeable, can be reversed as a fraudulent transfer and can expose the people involved to liability. paratum's work is preventive and is done with counsel who will stand behind it. if a dispute is already underway, the right first call is to litigation counsel. frequently asked questions who should consider pre-litigation planning? physicians, executives, business owners, real estate investors and anyone whose wealth or work creates meaningful liability exposure. when should it begin? before any claim arises or is reasonably foreseeable. planning done early is more flexible and far more durable. can assets be moved after a lawsuit is filed? transfers made to hinder, delay or defraud a creditor can be reversed and can create additional liability. an existing dispute should be taken to litigation counsel. does paratum provide litigation defense? no. paratum s role is preventive planning and coordination. legal representation is provided by independent licensed attorneys. not legal advice. see disclosures . family office

title: Wealth Management Oversight & Merchant Banking for Family Offices
desc: Family office services from Paratum: oversight of the advisers and managers who invest a family's capital, merchant banking for family office transactions, and family office setup.
text: family office paratum's family office work grew out of necessity. once a family's structures were in place, it asked paratum to oversee the capital inside them. wealth management oversight paratum helps families set an investment policy, select and monitor the registered investment advisers and managers who invest their capital, and see the whole of it in consolidated reporting. it does not manage money itself, which lets it judge the managers who do. merchant banking family offices increasingly invest directly in real estate, operating companies and energy. paratum helps source and structure those transactions, arranges debt and equity alongside the family's own capital with lenders and registered firms, and brings in co-investors where a deal is larger than one family should take alone. family office formation for families forming a single-family office, paratum coordinates the entity structure, governance, staffing and the outside providers it relies on. our role paratum brings together the professionals and institutions a family relies on and keeps a single view across all of them. investment management is performed by registered investment advisers and qualified managers; securities transactions by registered firms. frequently asked questions does paratum manage investments? no. investment management is performed by independent registered investment advisers and managers. paratum helps select and oversee them. can paratum work with an existing family office? yes. paratum provides structuring, transaction and coordination support alongside a family office s existing staff and advisers. can paratum help form a single-family office? yes. paratum coordinates the legal, organizational and operational work of forming one, including governance and the choice of outside providers. paratum is not a registered investment adviser or broker-dealer. see disclosures . people

title: Case Studies
desc: Anonymized examples of how Paratum has structured tax, protection and succession strategies for clients in complex situations.
text: case studies client names are never published. each case is described in general terms, with details changed to protect confidentiality. a founder’s sale situation the founder of a profitable services company expected an eight-figure sale within two years, almost all of it taxable in one year in a high-tax state. structure shares were moved into non-grantor and dynasty trusts before a buyer set the value, part of the price was taken as rollover equity, and part of the remaining gain was offset with direct energy investments. outcome tax on the sale was reduced and partly deferred, and much of the future growth sits outside the founder’s estate. stranded losses situation a holding company carried large net operating losses from a business it had wound down, with no income left to use them against. structure paratum found a profitable private business and coordinated a merger structured within the section 382 limits, with tax counsel and valuation advisers. outcome the losses offset the combined company’s income over the following years and were reflected in the terms of the merger. a surgeon’s exposure situation a surgeon with high income held rental properties and a brokerage account in his own name, all reachable by a malpractice claim. structure each property moved into its own llc, equity was stripped with documented financing, liquid assets went into a domestic asset protection trust, and a ppli policy held part of the portfolio. outcome exposed assets were separated and protected years before any claim, and the portfolio’s annual tax fell. illustrative examples. knowledge

title: Knowledge: Tax Strategy, Asset Protection, Trusts & M&A
desc: Paratum Knowledge: reference articles and answers on tax strategy, asset protection, offshore and domestic trusts, estate planning, retirement accounts and tax-efficient M&A.
text: knowledge knowledge for complex wealth. independent perspectives on taxation, asset protection, strategic transactions and the preservation of wealth. every article cites its primary sources and is reviewed before publication; see our editorial standards . m a and transactions draft · review pending can net operating losses be monetized? net operating losses cannot be sold on their own, but transactions can let a profitable business use them, within the limits of sections 172, 269, 382, 383 and 384 and the economic substance doctrine. read retirement accounts draft · review pending solo 401(k) vs. self-directed ira, and when roth makes sense how a solo 401(k) and a self-directed ira differ on eligibility, contribution limits, investments, loans, leveraged real estate, prohibited transactions and creditor protection, and the trade-offs of the roth versions of each. read trusts and estate planning draft · review pending revocable vs. irrevocable trusts what each kind of trust does and does not do for probate, control, creditor protection, estate tax and income tax, and why irrevocability alone does not guarantee estate exclusion or protection. read asset protection draft · review pending five commonly considered asset protection trust states compared nevada, south dakota, delaware, alaska and wyoming compared on limitation periods, exception creditors, taxes, trust duration and privacy, with the limits every domestic asset protection trust shares. read draft · review pending equity stripping: how it works and where it fails how encumbering an asset with genuine, documented debt affects what a judgment creditor can reach, the legal limits under voidable transfer and bankruptcy law, and why the borrowed funds remain the borrower s assets. read offshore planning draft · review pending offshore asset protection trusts: cook islands, nevis, belize, cayman, gibraltar and others compared how the jurisdictions most often discussed for offshore trusts compare on limitation periods, burden of proof, treatment of foreign judgments, cost and track record, with the limits u.s. courts impose and the u.s. reporting every offshore trust requires. read tax strategy draft · review pending charitable giving strategies compared: from donor-advised funds to nimcruts outright gifts, appreciated stock, donor-advised funds, private foundations, charitable remainder trusts including the nimcrut and flip unitrust, lead trusts, gift annuities and ira gifts, with the 2026 rule changes. read frequently asked questions the firm what does paratum do? paratum designs tax, asset protection, succession and transaction strategies for families, business owners and family offices, then selects and coordinates the attorneys, cpas, trustees, advisers, banks and carriers who implement them, and manages those relationships over time. how is paratum paid? paratum’s fees are agreed in writing at the start of each engagement. specialists are engaged and paid directly by the client. do you replace my attorney or cpa? no. paratum works alongside a client’s existing advisers and keeps them informed. where a specialist is needed who is not already involved, paratum introduces one. who carries out the legal and tax work? licensed professionals. paratum is not a law firm, accounting firm, investment adviser, broker-dealer or insurance agency; attorneys, cpas, registered firms and licensed agents engaged by the client do that work. strategies what is the difference between tax mitigation and deferral? mitigation reduces the tax owed. deferral moves it to a later year, keeping the capital working in the meantime. most strategies combine the two. how do oil and gas investments reduce taxes? qualifying intangible drilling and development costs may be deductible in the year paid or incurred, subject to applicable elections and limitations. certain working interests can generate nonpassive losses under section 469(c)(3), but the ownership structure (including whether liability is limited), the investor's basis and amount at risk, and other rules determine how much of those losses can offset other income. production income may be partly sheltered by depletion, which has its own limits. what is ppli? private placement life insurance holds an investment portfolio inside a life insurance policy. if the policy meets the tax code's definition of life insurance and its diversification and investor control requirements, growth is not currently taxed and the death benefit is generally free of income tax under section 101. estate tax is a separate question, usually addressed by having a trust own the policy. loans, withdrawals, surrenders, lapses and modified endowment contract status can each produce different tax results. it suits investors with substantial assets and a long horizon. what are tax attributes, and how can they be monetized? tax attributes are tax assets a company carries, such as net operating losses, loss carryforwards and credits. they are realized through a merger, acquisition or restructuring that lets a profitable business use them, within the section 382 limits, and some credits can be sold for cash. what is an asset protection trust? an irrevocable trust, in a state such as nevada or south dakota or a jurisdiction such as the cook islands, that protects assets from future creditors while the person who funded it can remain a discretionary beneficiary. is equity stripping legal? yes, when it uses real, documented obligations on commercial terms and is done before any claim exists. arrangements that exist only on paper, or are put in place to defeat a known creditor, can be disregarded. when is it too late to protect assets? once a claim exists or is reasonably foreseeable, new transfers can be reversed as fraudulent. protection should be in place years before it is needed. working together how confidential is it? client names are never published, and information is shared with specialists only as an engagement requires. discretion is the product. what happens in a first conversation? an unhurried discussion of your position and goals. nothing needs to be prepared, and there is no obligation. do you work with clients outside california? yes. paratum works with clients across the united states and on four continents. contact
